definitions.explanation: A carved wooden mask worn by performers in Noh theater. Figuratively, an expressionless face.

examples.japanese: {能面|のうめん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦{舞|ま}う→舞う：04573_mau⟧。
examples.english: To dance wearing a Noh mask.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{能面|のうめん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}→江戸時代：20431_edojidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{作|つく}られた→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: This Noh mask was made in the Edo period.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{能面|のうめん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{表情|ひょうじょう}→表情：03585_hyoujou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いていた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: She listened to the story with a face as expressionless as a Noh mask.

notes:
A carved wooden mask used in ⟦{能|のう}→能：01927_nou⟧ (Noh theater). Different mask types represent fixed roles such as young women, old men, and demons.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {能面|のうめん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to put on a Noh mask
- {能面|のうめん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧: an expressionless face

CULTURAL NOTE:
A skilled Noh actor can make a single mask seem to change emotion by tilting the head, since its carved expression is deliberately neutral. This is why {能面|のうめん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧よう describes a blank, unreadable face.
